To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) soil temperature best predicts CHF fluxes and explained > 90% of the variability, (2) water table depth has a non‐linear impact on CH4 flux, and (3) CH4 emissions are driven by temperature rather than by NEE or carbon supply.

(1) the major driver of CH4 fluxes is soil temperature, (2) the effect of water table depth on CH4 flux is complex and nonlinear, and (3) CH4 fluxes are not driven by NEE and are not limited to labile carbon supply.

(i) CH4 fluxes from the tundra in the Alaskan arctic are driven by soil temperature and (ii) water table height has a nonlinear impact, increasing CH4 efflux as water table height decreases below the soil surface, but decreasing CH4 efflux when water table height increases above the soil surface.
